slides.prompt: Part 5 Gapped Text: choose the sentence that makes the ideas flow.
slides.hint: Two stories today: the light bulb, and fast travel.
slides.notes: SET INDUCTION. 60-min Tue lesson 8 Sep 2026, sl_t3 17:50-18:50. Say: 'Eight sentences fell out of two stories. Our job: put back the one that makes the ideas flow.' Module pp.36-37 gapped text (P1P5, marks collected). Outcomes (teacher-kept): use the 4 checks on every gap; complete gaps 1-8 in books. 1M: noisy class, no roles or competitions; fingers vote + brief partner talk only.

slides.prompt: Read Edison's story. One sentence is missing.
slides.text: Edison wanted a bulb that lasted a long time. [ GAP ] Finally, his new bulb burned for many hours. Vote next: 1 finger for A, 2 for B, 3 for C.
slides.notes: Set induction continues. Read the story aloud, point at the gap. Then move to the vote.

slides.prompt: Edison's story. Which sentence is BEST?
options: He tested thousands of materials, one after another.
His laboratory was a large building in America.
Many people use bright lamps today.
slides.answer: He tested thousands of materials, one after another.
slides.feedback: A connects his goal to the result. B fits the topic, but it does not explain the result.
slides.hint: Are B and C bad English?
slides.notes: TEST the whole job by instinct before teaching the checks. Fingers vote, then reveal. Say: 'No — good English, wrong job. C fits lamps, but it does not connect his goal and result.'

slides.prompt: Check 1: what are we talking about?
slides.text: Topic words: bulbs, wires, bright rooms, safe light. Hakim joined the school science club last month. [ GAP ] He now enjoys building simple machines with his friends.
slides.notes: INTRODUCE Check 1 (topic). Say: 'First ask: what are we talking about? Circle the topic words with me.' Do not vote yet.

slides.prompt: Hakim's story. Which sentences survive the topic check?
slides.answer: All three survive: each fits Hakim or the club.
slides.feedback: Topic is a first filter, not the final answer.
slides.notes: TEST Check 1. Take a fingers vote first (A: club taught him; B: sister draws pictures; C: learnt the tools safely), then reveal: all three survive, so topic alone cannot finish the job.

slides.prompt: Check 2: who or what are we following?
slides.text: Chain it: Mei → she. Kitten → it. Mei brought home a small kitten. [ GAP ] Soon it slept in a warm box beside her bed.
slides.notes: INTRODUCE Check 2 (who/what chain). Point at each link as you say it: Mei to she, kitten to it.

slides.prompt: Mei's story. Which one is BEST?
options: She fed it milk every morning.
slides.answer: She fed it milk every morning.
slides.feedback: A: Mei → she; kitten → it. We follow the same pair.
slides.hint: Who is she? What is it?
slides.notes: TEST Check 2. Fingers vote, then reveal. Say: 'B is about kittens, but it drops THIS kitten. C drops them both.'

slides.prompt: Check 3: do not read only the gap.
slides.text: Read BEFORE. Read AFTER. Razak had an important bus to catch that morning. [ GAP ] Luckily, the driver waited and he reached school on time.
slides.notes: INTRODUCE Check 3 (both sides). The important one: cover the gap with your hand and show that neither side alone is enough.

slides.prompt: Razak's story. Which one is BEST?
options: Heavy rain flooded the road near his house.
Razak carried a heavy bag to school.
Buses in his town were usually blue.
slides.answer: Heavy rain flooded the road near his house.
slides.feedback: A bridges both sides: late bus, flood, driver waited.
slides.hint: Use the sentence before AND after the gap.
slides.notes: TEST Check 3. Fingers vote, then reveal. Say: 'B fits Razak, but it does not explain the waiting driver. C fits buses, but it connects to nothing.'

slides.prompt: Check 4: what kind of idea is missing?
slides.text: Predict first, then look at the choices. Lina dreamed of visiting her grandmother in seconds. [ GAP ] When she woke up, she smiled at the wonderful dream.
slides.notes: INTRODUCE Check 4 (predict before options). Partner talk 30 seconds: 'What probably happened in the middle?' Take two answers, then move to the vote.

slides.prompt: Lina's story. Which one is BEST?
options: In the dream, she used a glowing travel machine.
She liked eating noodles with her grandmother.
Travelling by car takes a long time.
slides.answer: In the dream, she used a glowing travel machine.
slides.feedback: A: dream trip, then awake smiling. B and C leave the dream.
slides.notes: TEST Check 4. Fingers vote, then reveal. Teleportation flavour links to Module p.37 without revealing answers.

slides.prompt: Trap: all three make sense. Why is only one best?
slides.text: The old inventor showed the pupils his first lamp. [ GAP ] The pupils clapped when the lamp lit up the dark room.
slides.notes: Read aloud, point at the gap. Let them feel all three fitting before the vote.

slides.prompt: The lamp story. Which one is BEST?
options: He had fixed its broken wire that morning.
Thomas Edison was a famous inventor.
The museum keeps many old lamps.
slides.answer: He had fixed its broken wire that morning.
slides.feedback: A links the lamp to the clapping. B shares a name but drops this lamp.
slides.hint: Same word? Wrong question. Which idea connects?
slides.notes: TEST the trap. Say: 'Don't ask same word. Ask: which idea connects?' C fits lamps, but it does not connect to the clapping pupils. Invention flavour links to Module p.36.

slides.prompt: Found a gap? What do you check?
slides.answer: 1. Topic: what is this part about? 2. Who: who follows who? 3. Both sides: what must join up? 4. Predict the idea, then choose.
slides.feedback: Only then: look at the choices. Do not hunt for one repeated word.
slides.notes: LESSON DEVELOPMENT close. Elicit the 4 checks orally first, then reveal to confirm. Leave this slide on screen during bookwork — come back to it while pupils work.

slides.answer: Gaps 1 to 4 use sentences A to D. Gaps 5 to 8 use sentences E to H.
slides.notes: Say: 'First story, first set. Second story, second set.' Then name it: open Module pages 36 and 37. Light Bulb p.36 + Teleportation p.37 (LS 3.1.1/3.1.2). No module answers on slides; books carry the marked activity.

slides.task: Do gaps 1 to 8. Use the 4 checks on every gap.
slides.frame: 1 Topic? 2 Who? 3 Both sides? 4 Predict, then choose.
slides.notes: ACTIVITY (teacher-specified: module bookwork). Say: 'Silent work. Show me the 4 checks on every gap.' About 20 min. P1P5, 8 marks. Collect books at the door.

slides.prompt: Without looking: what are the 4 checks?
slides.notes: Exit evidence, 2 min: eyes off the screen, tell your partner. Gaps in recall reopen next lesson.
